common_name: Marlot Skimmia (Compact Fragrant Male Pollinator Shrub)

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring or fall into moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in shade to partial shade, and place within roughly 15-20 feet of female cultivars such as 'Nymans', 'Rubella', or 'Temptation' to ensure reliable berry set on those plants.

directions: An RHS Award of Garden Merit male selection also sold under the older name 'Godrie's Dwarf', Marlot forms a dense, rounded mound of glossy dark-green evergreen leaves and is grown chiefly for its ornamental value and pollinating power rather than berries. Reddish-pink winter flower buds cluster at the branch tips through the cold months before opening in mid- to late spring into fragrant, pink-flushed white flowers that draw early pollinators. Because it is male it never fruits, but a single well-placed plant can pollinate multiple female Skimmia japonica shrubs over a wide area, making it a workhorse companion for berry-producing cultivars. Grow it in consistently moist, acidic, well-drained soil in shade to part shade, mulch to conserve moisture, and prune only lightly right after flowering since next year's buds form quickly on the current season's growth.
